primitives.name: Play Execution Fidelity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Now comes a most difficult act for any captain, namely, the elimination of all plays that are not sufficiently well executed by his men to be classed on the average as successful plays.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{exec}': 'dimensionless normalized execution score (0 to 1)', 'P_{play}': 'set of plays indexed by i'}
primitives.assumptions: Plays are independently evaluated based on historical success rate and team proficiency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F_exec < threshold, play is excluded from critical game set.

layer2.mapping: F_exec is derived from empirical play outcome distribution, used as kernel for Bayesian model selection in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Historical play success rate per team member

primitives.name: Opponent Discipline Factor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Many plays that are peculiarly successful against weaker teams are, from their very nature, useless against well-disciplined opponents.
primitives.assumptions: Discipline is inversely correlated with susceptibility to high-risk, low-fidelity plays.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D_opp > threshold, certain plays are deemed non-robust.

layer2.mapping: D_opp maps to a probabilistic constraint in GSE's state-space pruning algorithm.

primitives.name: Play Risk Exhaustion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Certain ones of them must be given up because they would risk the loss of the ball; and others because they would needlessly exhaust the men.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{risk}': 'dimensionless risk score (0 to 1)', 'E_{effort}': 'normalized energy expenditure per play'}
primitives.assumptions: Risk and effort are additive penalties in strategic decision-making.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_risk + E_effort > threshold, play is eliminated.

layer2.mapping: Combined risk-effort metric is used in GSE's cost function for play selection.
layer2.telemetry: Ball possession duration and player fatigue indices

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that strategic play selection is a constrained optimization problem under two primary regimes: execution fidelity and opponent discipline. Execution fidelity (F_exec) is a scalar measure of how consistently a play is performed, derived from historical data. Opponent discipline (D_opp) modulates the efficacy of a play—plays that succeed against weak teams may fail against disciplined ones due to predictable behavioral responses. These two factors form a dual constraint in GSI’s Bayesian framework, where each play is scored as P(play|team, opponent), and filtered through a posterior probability threshold. In GSE, this manifests as a state transition system where each play is evaluated against a composite utility function U(play) = f(F_exec, D_opp, R_risk, E_effort). The failure mode occurs when either fidelity or discipline is misestimated, leading to overconfidence in ineffective strategies. This leads to a recursive refinement process where the captain iteratively prunes plays based on empirical feedback, aligning with a Bayesian updating mechanism.
